title: The repo ships five standalone compose files — one per release channel plus a postgres-free PGlite variant — that pull pre-built images and expose the same loopback ports, so only one stack runs at a time
content:
| File | Project name | Image tag | Backend |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `docker-compose.yml` | `powerhouse` | `latest` | postgres |
| `docker-compose.dev.yml` | `powerhouse-dev` | `dev` | postgres |
| `docker-compose.test.yml` | `powerhouse-test` | `rc` | postgres |
| `docker-compose.staging.yml` | `powerhouse-staging` | `staging` | postgres |
| `docker-compose.pglite.yml` | `powerhouse-pglite` | `latest` | embedded PGlite |

Nothing is built locally: every file pulls pre-built images from `cr.vetra.io`. The files are **standalone** (no `include` / `extends`) because compose `include` cannot partially override an included service (same-name conflict) and each file must work on its own (`docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d`). A per-file project `name:` gives each stack its own network — a shared fixed network would collide on the `postgres` alias across stacks.

Every stack exposes the same services on the same loopback ports, so the stacks are **mutually exclusive while running**:

| Service | Host (127.0.0.1) | Container |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connect | 3000 | 3001 |
| Switchboard | 4000 | 3000 |
| Postgres | 5444 | 5432 |

The Connect UI is pre-wired to the local Switchboard through `PH_CONNECT_CONFIG_JSON` = `{"connect":{"drives":{"defaultDrives":[{"url":"http://localhost:4000",…}]}}}`, so the SPA auto-adds the remote drive on boot — and the first default drive's origin also configures the attachment service. Switchboard gets both storage URLs pointed at the single `postgres:16.1` service (named volume `postgres_data`), depends on it being healthy, and every service has a health check. The PGlite variant drops the postgres service and both DB variables and mounts a volume at `/app/.ph`; it is a local-dev convenience, not a deployment shape. `docker compose down` keeps the named volumes; `down -v` deletes them. The previous single `docker-compose.yml` had been stale since the March redesign: wrong registry, wrong container ports (`:3000:4000` / `:4000:4001`), ineffective env vars, no connect→switchboard wiring and no data volume.
